title: Finite-free scalar extension and a counit-normalized right-adjoint mate
statement:
Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings with an $A$-basis $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ of $B$. Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites, use constant coefficient module derived categories, and let $T_{\mathcal C},T_{\mathcal D}$ and $U_{\mathcal C},U_{\mathcal D}$ be derived scalar extension and restriction [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Let $F_R:D(\mathcal C,R)\to D(\mathcal D,R)$ and $G_R:D(\mathcal D,R)\to D(\mathcal C,R)$ be additive functors with specified adjunctions $F_R\dashv G_R$ (natural Hom bijections with units and counits satisfying the triangle identities), counits $\varepsilon_R$, for $R=A,B$. Require $G_B$ to preserve coefficient multiplication: $G_B(a\,\mathrm{id}_N)=a\,\mathrm{id}_{G_BN}$ for every $a\in B$ and $N\in D(\mathcal D,B)$ (in particular this holds for a $B$-linear functor). Suppose there is a natural isomorphism
$$c:T_{\mathcal D}F_A\xrightarrow{\sim}F_BT_{\mathcal C}.$$
Require its restriction normalization: there is a natural identification $U_{\mathcal D}F_B\cong F_AU_{\mathcal C}$ under which $U_{\mathcal D}(c_P)$ is the finite-sum comparison $(F_AP)^{\oplus r}\to F_A(P^{\oplus r})$, with components $F_A$ of the basis inclusions.

The natural representing isomorphism $\theta_N:U_{\mathcal C}G_BN\xrightarrow{\sim}G_AU_{\mathcal D}N$ is characterized by the successive adjunction bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,U_{\mathcal C}G_BN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_B(T_{\mathcal C}P,G_BN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_B(F_BT_{\mathcal C}P,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_B(T_{\mathcal D}F_AP,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(F_AP,U_{\mathcal D}N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,G_AU_{\mathcal D}N).$$
Define $b_M:T_{\mathcal C}G_AM\to G_BT_{\mathcal D}M$ as the $F_B\dashv G_B$ transpose of $T_{\mathcal D}(\varepsilon_{A,M})\circ c_{G_AM}^{-1}$. Then $b_M$ is a natural isomorphism and
$$\varepsilon_{B,T_{\mathcal D}M}\circ F_B(b_M)=T_{\mathcal D}(\varepsilon_{A,M})\circ c_{G_AM}^{-1}.$$
Under $\theta_{T_{\mathcal D}M}$ and $UT\cong(-)^{\oplus r}$, its restriction is the finite-sum comparison $(G_AM)^{\oplus r}\to G_A(M^{\oplus r})$ with $j$-th component $G_A$ of the $j$-th inclusion and inverse given by $G_A$ of the projections. The resulting $B$-linear map is independent of the basis used to verify invertibility.

proof.text: Construct scalar extension as sheafified ordinary extension of scalars. The given finite basis makes the module extension functor exact. At each object of the site, the ordinary module basis theorem identifies the direct sum with restriction of extension; the sheaf adjunction unit has exactly these columns. Evaluate cochain complexes degreewise to obtain the same isomorphism on complexes. Localize the exact adjunction: its unit formula and the two functor comparison isomorphisms transport the columns to the derived category. Every derived object has a complex representative, so the basis desc is invertible everywhere. Its inverse gives the required coordinates. The comparison isomorphism exhibits this exact extension as its left derived functor. Restriction reflects isomorphisms on sheaves objectwise, and on derived categories by homology.

proof.text: Compose the scalar and given adjunctions, transporting the second left adjoint along c. Their rightAdjointUniq isomorphism is theta. The characterization of rightAdjointUniq by the counit, followed by naturality of the Hom equivalences, gives exactly the displayed fivefold Hom chain.

proof.text: The categorical mate of c inverse has the stated counit equation by mateEquiv_counit. Applying the inverse Hom equivalence to that equation proves uniqueness. Each component is a B-linear derived morphism, and the multiplication hypothesis identifies multiplication on G_B with its image under G_B.

proof.text: Apply the Hom-chain characterization of theta to the composite of the scalar unit with U(b). The first adjunction gives b, the B-adjunction gives its counit expression, and precomposition by c cancels c inverse. Naturality of the second scalar unit and the A-adjunction triangle identity give theta U(b) eta_C = G_A(eta_D).

proof.text: For every basis element, commute multiplication through the B-linear component b, use the multiplication hypothesis on G_B, and apply naturality of theta. Substitute the preceding unit identity and the basis-column equations of the two scalar presentations. The resulting column is exactly G_A of the corresponding biproduct inclusion.

proof.text: The functorial biproduct isomorphism of the additive functor G_A gives inverse maps desc(G_A iota_j) and lift(G_A pi_j), including for the empty basis. The column computation conjugates U(b) to this isomorphism. Derived restriction reflects isomorphisms, hence every component b is invertible and the natural transformation is an isomorphism. The counit uniqueness result is independent of the basis.

Theta is constructed by rightAdjointUniq of the composed adjunctions; the mate is constructed by mateEquiv without a basis. The counit uniqueness clause expresses basis independence. Coefficient and module universes are the common max of site sizes and ring size, and the chosen derived Hom universe w remains independent.
